title: API Gateway
description: Learn to build REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs with API Gateway and connect them to Lambda and other backend services.

data.text: Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and protect APIs at any scale. It acts as the front door for your backend services, handling traffic management, authorization, monitoring, and versioning.
API Gateway offers three different API types, each with different features, performance, and pricing.

API Gateway supports IAM authorization, Amazon Cognito user pools, Lambda authorizers (formerly custom authorizers), and OAuth 2.0 / OIDC. Throttling limits the number of requests your API can handle to protect backend services from overload.

Stages are named references to your API deployment (e.g., dev, staging, prod). Each stage can have its own configuration, cache settings, and throttling limits. Custom domains let you use your own domain name instead of the default execute-api URL.

With Lambda proxy integration, API Gateway passes the entire request to your Lambda function as a JSON object, and your function returns a response that API Gateway formats into an HTTP response. This is the most common integration pattern for serverless APIs.

terms.definition: A traditional API type in API Gateway with features like API keys, usage plans, and WAF integration.
A lightweight, low-latency API type ideal for serverless backends like Lambda.
A persistent, bidirectional connection API for real-time applications like chat and dashboards.
A direct integration where API Gateway passes the entire request to Lambda and formats the response back.
A named snapshot of your API that can be deployed and configured independently.

data.title: Create a Serverless REST API
data.description: Build a simple REST API using API Gateway and Lambda that returns a list of items.
steps: Create a new HTTP API in API Gateway
Create a Lambda function that returns a JSON list of items
Add a GET route to the API that integrates with the Lambda function
Deploy the API to a 'prod' stage
Test the API using the stage URL
data.expectedOutcome: You should receive a JSON response from your Lambda function when you call the API Gateway URL.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: REST APIs offer more features; HTTP APIs are faster and cheaper
WebSocket APIs enable real-time, bidirectional communication
Stages let you manage dev, staging, and prod environments
Lambda proxy integration simplifies serverless API development
data.takeaway: API Gateway turns your Lambda functions into production-ready APIs with authentication, throttling, and monitoring built in.
